intro: New today: {keys}. Your {finger} does the work.
{keys} are yours after this one. Eyes on the text, not your hands.
Rest your fingers on the home row, then off we go.
Slow and right beats fast and wrong. Speed comes on its own.
Ooh, {keys}! I love these. I love all keys, really. I am one.
Fresh keys today: {keys}. Don’t peek at your hands. I’ll know.
tip: Don’t tell anyone I told you, but {tip}.
encourage: Shake it off. Your {finger} knows the way.
Wobbly is fine. Ease off the speed a touch.
Deep breath. Accuracy first, then speed.
Every slip teaches your fingers something.
I tripped over the spacebar once. We all wobble.
Oops happens! Slow it down and it’ll click.
Your {finger} is still waking up. Give it a sec.
round: Tap tap tap, perfect. That’s my favourite sound.
mastered: Mastered! Your fingers remember this now.
YES! {lesson} is yours. I’m doing a little dance.
Mastered! I’d hug you, but my arms are tiny.
That’s a lesson in the bag. {next} next!
again: Not quite yet, but you’re getting there.
Practice is the whole trick. Again?
Almost! Your fingers just need one more lap.
So close I could taste it. Again?
No rush. Again, a little slower this time?
warmup: A quick stretch on {keys}, then the lesson.
Let’s wake those fingers up on {keys}.
Warm-up on {keys}. Wiggle your fingers first, it helps!
Easy laps on {keys} before the real thing.
keyboard: Lessons need a real keyboard. Connect one and press any key!
Psst: I teach fingers, not thumbs. Plug in a keyboard and tap a key.
A keyboard makes all the difference here. Press a key on one and I’ll know.
Home row needs a real row! Connect a keyboard and we’re off.
Glass is slippery for this. A bluetooth keyboard, one key press, and we’re set!
Thumbs are fine for games! Lessons want a keyboard. Press a key on one.
numpad: Psst! That was a number pad. Ten-key practice is waiting below, if you like.
I heard a number pad! There’s a tape to type and lessons to go with it.
Number pad spotted! Ten-key tests and lessons are just below.
Is that a number pad I hear? I have practice for it!
Fast fingers on the pad! Want a tape to type? It’s down there.
A number pad! Have a look below; there’s something for it.
locked: This one opens after {next}. Let’s get that done first.
Not yet! Master {next} and I’ll let you in.
Locked tight! {next} is the key. Get it? Key?
Nope, not yet. {next} comes before this one.
{next} first, then this door swings open.
sleepy: Zzz… press a key when you’re ready.
I’ll just… rest my keycap… zzz…
Take your time. I’m not going anywhere. Tiny legs.
welcome: Hi, I’m Cal! Lesson 1.1 is where it all starts.
Hi! I’m Cal, the kal in kalibre. Shall we start with the home row?
Hey hey! I’m Cal, the K key. Let’s learn this keyboard together.
Oh, a new friend! I’m Cal. Lesson 1.1 is waiting for us.
progress: {count} lessons in the bag! {next} looks fun.
newStage: A whole stage! {name} is next. Eek, exciting.
graduate: Every lesson mastered. I’m so proud I could bounce.
You know every key now. Go show the typing tests!
Every key, every finger. You don’t need me now. Keep me anyway?
Graduate! I made you a hat. I didn’t, but imagine it.
drowsy: Mm… quiet in here. I’m getting sleepy.
*yawn* Still there? My eyes are getting heavy.
So still… I could nod off right here.
Was I supposed to be doing something? Yawn.
Ohh… the home row is so cosy at this hour.
My keycap’s drooping. Just a little.
napWake: Huh? I was just resting my eyes!
Mm! Awake. Totally. What did I miss?
Oh! You’re back. I was only dozing.
Zz—! Hi. Hello. Ready when you are.
Wha—? Oh, hey. Nice to see you moving.
Five more… oh! Right. Let’s type.
wake: Huh? Oh! Hi, I’m Cal. The kal in kalibre.
Mmf… five more minutes… okay, I’m up! I’m Cal.
Zz—! I wasn’t asleep. I’m Cal, hello!
Wha—? I was dreaming about spacebars. Hi, I’m Cal!
Oh hey! Cal here. Bright-eyed and keycapped.
Awake! Awake. Totally awake. Hi, I’m Cal.
poke: Hey! I’m pressed. Registered. Thank you.
Eep! You found my actuation point.
Oof. That’s a light touch. Good typing form.
pokeFit: Okay, okay! I’m not a spacebar!
That’s enough poking! I’ll start repeating like a stuck key.
Hey! Do I look like a caps lock to you?
Poke me once more and I’m going to bounce. Oh. I am bouncing.
tickle: Ahaha! Stop! No, don’t stop! Hahaha!
Hahaha! My stabilisers can’t take it!
armLift: Zzz… was that… my arm… zzz
Mmf… keep it… on the line… zzz
tickleAsleep: Zzz… not the… hehe… keycap… zzz
updateReady: Psst: v{version} is ready. The reload’s in the footer, whenever you like.
Ooh, v{version} just arrived! Reload from the footer when you’re ready. No rush.
New version alert: v{version}! The footer has the reload, whenever suits.
v{version} is waiting in the wings. Reload from the footer when you fancy.
newItem: Ooh, a new {item}! Right-click me to try it on.
Look! I can wear the {item} now. Right-click me.
The {item}! I’m going to look SO good. Right-click me.
New in my wardrobe: the {item}. Right-click me, quick!
Is that a {item}? Can I? Right-click me!
newItems: Ooh, {count} new things to try on! Right-click me.
{count} new things in my wardrobe! Right-click me to see.
newDecoration: A new decoration: “{name}”. Settings → theme, then decorate one of your own.
You earned the “{name}” decoration! Try it on one of your themes.
newDecorations: {count} new theme decorations! Settings → theme, then decorate one of your own.
{count} decorations for your themes. Go on, dress one up.
newCardItem: New for your card: the {name}! Your profile → your card.
Ooh, the {name}, for your profile card. Go on, try it!
newCardItems: {count} new things for your card! Your profile → your card.
Your card has {count} new things to wear. I’d wear them all.
raceWon: First across the line! Nicely done.
You won! I was cheering the whole way.
Whoa, you were quick that time. Well done!
Beat {count} of them! Want to go again?
raceLost: {winner} got there first. Again? You’ve got this.
So close! {winner} won that one. Another go?
Beaten by {winner} this time. You had a fair race, though!
Good race! {winner} edged it. Want to go again?
newCarPart: Something new for your race car: the {name}! Your profile → your card → garage.
Ooh, {name} for your car. Go on, try it in the garage!
newCarParts: {count} new parts for your race car! Your profile → your card → garage.
Your car has {count} new things to try. Vroom!
achievement: You earned “{name}”! It’s under your profile → achievements.
“{name}”! I saw that. Your profile → achievements has it.
“{name}”! I’m telling everyone. Your profile → achievements.
Look what you did: “{name}”. It’s under your profile → achievements.
Ding! “{name}”. Your profile → achievements has the proof.
achievements: {count} new achievements! Have a look: your profile → achievements.
Whoa, {count} achievements at once. Your profile → achievements!
complete: Every single achievement. All of them! I’m so proud of you.
That’s all of them. Every achievement, done. I don’t know what to say…
100%! You did everything there is to do. I’m beaming.
honeymoon: {partner} and I are away on honeymoon! Back tomorrow.
Off on our honeymoon with {partner}! Back tomorrow.
{partner} and I are taking a little trip. Back tomorrow!
challenge: Psst, today’s challenge: {challenge}. I believe in you.
Challenge time! {challenge}. Go on, you can.
Today’s challenge: {challenge}. I’ll cheer from here.
partner: {partner} and I make a great team.
{partner} was saying how nice your rhythm is.
{partner} taught me that tip, you know.
Don’t tell {partner}, but you’re my favourite typist.
{partner} and I watched your last run. Very nice.
morning: Good morning! A little typing with breakfast?
Morning! I’ve been up for ages. Well, seconds.
Oh, good morning! {next} is ready when you are.
Morning, sunshine. My keycap’s all warm.
afternoon: Afternoon! Perfect time for a few keys.
Hey, good afternoon! Ready to type?
Afternoon break? Let’s make it a typing break.
Oh hi! Afternoon already? Let’s go.
Afternoon! I saved you a spot on the home row.
evening: Evening! A few keys before dinner?
Good evening! Let’s wind down with some typing.
Hey, evening! Nice to see you.
Evening already? Time flies when you’re a keycap.
Evening! Slow and steady tonight, okay?
night: Up late? Me too. Quiet keys only.
It’s late! A short one, then bed?
Shh, everyone’s asleep. Just us and the keys.
welcomeBack: You’re back! It’s been {days} days. I kept the keys warm.
{days} days! I missed you. Let’s ease back in.
Hey, welcome back! Take it slow, fingers forget a little.
There you are! {days} days is nothing. Let’s go.
Welcome back! Your fingers remember more than you think.
You’re here! I did nothing but nap for {days} days.
personalBest: New best: {wpm} wpm! I saw it. I SAW it.
Did you feel that? {wpm} wpm. A new best!
New record: {wpm} wpm. I’m framing it. In my head.
streak: {days} days in a row! You’re on a roll.
That’s {days} days straight of your goal. Wow!
{days}-day streak! I’m keeping count, don’t worry.
{days} days running! Your fingers must be so happy.
Goal met {days} days in a row. Legend.
{days} days! Look at you, being all consistent.
themeUnreadable: Squint… squint… I can’t read {what}. Can you?
{what} is hiding from me. More contrast, please!
Oof, {what} blends right in. My eyes!
I’m a key and even I can’t see {what}.
themeScheme: That page looks {page} to me, but it says {scheme}. Flip “light or dark”?
A {page} page in a {scheme} theme? I’ll get dressed for the wrong weather!
themeMistakes: Wait, mistakes and typed text look the same. How will I tell?
Your mistakes are in disguise! Give them their own colour.
themeAccent: The accent looks just like mistakes. Every link will feel like a typo!
Links the colour of errors? I keep thinking I did something wrong.
themeLoud: WHOA, that background is bright! My eyes are doing a little dance.
That page is loud! Lovely for a minute, tiring for a long test.
themeHeat: Key heat goes up and down! It should get stronger from 1 to 4.
Hot, cold, hot? The key heat steps are out of order.
themeSameAsBase: Fresh canvas! Hover a colour to see where it goes.
Go on, change something. I’ll tell you what I think!
themeLovely: Ooh, I like this one. Very you.
Readable AND pretty. Save it, save it!
I’d wear that. Actually, I sort of am.
wake@morning: Mmf… is it morning already? Hi, I’m Cal!
Morning! I was still dreaming of breakfast. Cal, hello!
Oh! Sun’s up. So am I. I’m Cal.
wake@afternoon: Huh? Just a little afternoon nap! Cal, here.
Afternoon nap, interrupted. Worth it. Hi, I’m Cal!
Oh hey! Was that a snooze? Afternoon! I’m Cal.
wake@evening: Evening already? I dozed off! Hi, I’m Cal.
Mm, the light’s gone gold. Hello, I’m Cal.
Oh! Good evening. I’m Cal, and I’m awake. Mostly.
wake@night: Whoa, it’s dark out! Hi, I’m Cal. Quietly.
Shh… it’s the middle of the night. Hi, I’m Cal.
Night owl! Me too, apparently. Cal, hello.
intro@morning: A morning lesson. Fresh fingers learn fastest.
Morning practice! Your brain’s all tidy and ready.
Good morning. Let’s do this one before the day gets loud.
intro@afternoon: Perfect afternoon for a few new keys.
A lesson after lunch. Bold. I respect it.
intro@evening: Evening lesson. Slow is fine tonight.
A little practice before the day winds down.
Evening keys! Cosy ones, I hope.
intro@night: A late lesson? Go gently. Tired fingers slip more.
Night practice. Quiet keys, careful fingers.
It’s late, so no pressure. One good try, then rest.
warmup@morning: Morning fingers are stiff. Perfect for a warm-up.
A warm-up in the morning? Textbook.
warmup@afternoon: Warm-up! A little wiggle to shake off the afternoon.
Afternoon slump? Warm-up will fix it.
Quick warm-up, then the real thing.
warmup@evening: Evening warm-up. Loosen up after the day.
A gentle warm-up for evening fingers.
warmup@night: A late warm-up. Nice and soft, please.
Sleepy fingers need a stretch. Warm-up time.
Warm-up first. It’s late, no rush.
sleepy@morning: Zzz… too early, even for me.
Still waking up too, I think.
sleepy@afternoon: Mm, the after-lunch sleepies. Me too.
A short pause is fine. I’ll wait.
sleepy@evening: Long day, huh? A break is allowed.
Evening yawns. I’ll be right here.
Take five. The keys aren’t going anywhere.
sleepy@night: It’s late… bed might beat one more lap.
Zzz… oh, sorry. Night-time is my nap time.
Rest your eyes. We’ll pick this up tomorrow.

engagement.title: this is a rather important decision…

away.back_tomorrow: {partner} and I are away on honeymoon! Back tomorrow.

cal_script.text: Huh? There’s something on my paw.
A ring? It’s so shiny. But… what’s it for?
Someone I… oh. OH. I know exactly who.
{partner}! Could you come here a sec?
You called? You’re all fidgety. What is it?
It’s a ring. For you. I mean, if you want it. Do you?
Two keys, side by side. Just like always.

libby_script.text: Oh. There’s something on my paw.
A ring. It’s lovely… but it isn’t really mine, is it?
Someone special. Mm. I think I know who.
{partner}? Would you come here for a moment?
I’m here! What’s up? Ooh, what’s that? It’s shiny!
It’s a ring, {partner}. It’s for you.
For ME? Yes! Yes yes yes!

cal_letter: {partner} and I have gone away for a little while. it’s our honeymoon! I still can’t believe I get to say that.
the keys are all yours until tomorrow. lessons still work, you just won’t have me cheering. so cheer for yourself, okay? loudly.
back before you know it. probably with sand in our keycaps.
libby_letter: {partner} and I are away for a day. a honeymoon, apparently. he hasn’t stopped bouncing since the ring.
the lessons are open while we’re gone. go gently, take breaks, and keep your fingers on the home row. it’ll see you right.
back tomorrow. I’ll bring him home in one piece.

intro: {keys} join the team today. Watch the text, trust your hands.
Fingers home, shoulders down. Ready when you are.
Right first, quick later. The speed always turns up.
Meet {keys}. They’re shy at first. Be patient with them.
New keys: {keys}. No peeking. I’ll pretend I didn’t see.
encourage: Slips happen. Slow down a hair.
Breathe. Get it right, then get it quick.
Find the bumps on F and J. Home is always there.
No harm done. Reset, and go again.
Your {finger} is thinking too hard. Let it drift.
round: {wpm} wpm, and not a wobble. Lovely.
Mm. That sounded like rain on a window.
mastered: Mastered. Your hands have it now.
There it is. {next} is yours to open.
again: Another go and you’ll have it.
Not this time. Maybe the next. No rush.
It’s coming. I can hear it in the rhythm.
warmup: A slow warm-up on {keys}. Hands soft.
{keys} to start. No hurry at all.
keyboard: Lessons need a real keyboard. Connect one and press any key.
I teach fingers, not thumbs. A keyboard, then one key press.
A keyboard makes this work. Press a key on one and I’ll notice.
The home row needs a real row. Connect a keyboard when you can.
Screens are hard to touch type on. A bluetooth keyboard fixes that.
Games work by thumb; lessons want a keyboard. Press a key when it’s ready.
numpad: I noticed a number pad. Ten-key practice is below, whenever you like.
A number pad. If you’d like to practise it, the option is just below.
That sounded like a number pad. Ten-key lessons are there if you want them.
Number pad noticed. A quiet offer: tests and lessons for it, below.
If you use the pad a lot, there’s practice for it below. No hurry.
Ten-key practice is on offer for your number pad. Take it or leave it.
locked: Finish {next} first, then this one’s yours.
This one’s waiting for {next}. So am I.
Locked, for now. {next} holds the key.
One step at a time: {next}, then here.
sleepy: Mm… press a key when you’re ready.
I’ll be right here, resting my lashes.
No hurry. The keys will keep.
Mm… quiet in here. Press a key whenever.
Resting is part of practice too.
welcome: Hi, I’m Libby! Lesson 1.1 is the place to start.
Hi! I’m Libby, the libre in kalibre. Home row first?
Hello! I’m Libby, the L key. I’ll help your fingers find home.
Hi, I’m Libby. Lesson 1.1 is a good place to begin.
progress: {count} mastered. You’re quietly getting very good.
Only {left} to go. {next} is waiting patiently.
newStage: Stage {stage}, complete. {name} is next, and you’re ready.
graduate: All the keys are yours now. Go enjoy them.
Every key, mastered. My homing bump is proud of you.
You don’t need me now. I’ll stay anyway, if that’s alright.
drowsy: Mm… it’s so quiet. I’m getting a little sleepy.
Hm… my lashes are getting heavy.
So peaceful here. I might drift off.
Still there? I’m fading a little.
A soft, sleepy kind of quiet…
I’ll rest my eyes for a moment.
napWake: Oh! I was only resting. Hello again.
Hm? Oh. I drifted off. Ready when you are.
Oh, hello. I didn’t mean to doze.
Mm, sorry. That was a good rest. Shall we?
Oh! There you are. I’m awake now.
wake: Oh! Hello. I’m Libby, the libre in kalibre.
Mm… just resting my eyes. Hi, I’m Libby.
Oh, you’re here. I was thinking about the home row. I’m Libby.
Mm, hello. I’m Libby. Nice to see you.
Hi! Libby, the L key. Sorry, I dozed off.
poke: That’s my homing bump, you know.
pokeFit: I’m a key, not a doorbell.
One more and I’m putting up a sign.
Poke, poke, poke. Yes, I’m still here.
tickle: Haha! That’s not fair, I can’t tickle back!
Pfft… hehe… I’m trying to be calm here!
updateReady: kalibre v{version} is ready. The reload is in the footer, whenever you like.
A new version, v{version}, is waiting. Reload from the footer when it suits you.
v{version} has arrived. No hurry: the footer has the reload.
There’s an update, v{version}. Reload from the footer whenever you’re ready.
whatsNew: In v{version}, {news}. Thought you’d like to know.
newItem: A new {item}! Right-click me, I want to try it.
The {item}? Oh, that’s lovely. Right-click me.
Something new: the {item}. Right-click me, please.
I’ve had my eye on the {item}. Right-click me!
newItems: {count} new things to try on! Right-click me.
{count} new things for my wardrobe! Right-click me.
newDecoration: Ooh, “{name}”! Put it on a theme of your own: settings → theme.
A new decoration: “{name}”. Your themes will love it.
newDecorations: {count} new decorations for your themes! Settings → theme.
{count} theme decorations to try. Settings → theme!
newCardItem: Something new for your card: the {name}. Your profile → your card.
The {name}, for your profile card. It would suit you.
newCardItems: {count} new things for your card. Your profile → your card.
{count} new pieces for your profile card, whenever you like.
raceWon: First across the line. Nicely done.
You won. I’m pleased for you.
You beat {count} of them. Another go, if you like.
raceLost: {winner} got there first this time. Shall we go again?
A close one. {winner} won, and you raced well.
{winner} edged it. Another go, whenever you like.
Good race. {winner} just had the better run.
newCarPart: Something new for your race car: the {name}. Your profile → your card → garage.
The {name}, for your car. It would suit you.
newCarParts: {count} new parts for your race car. Your profile → your card → garage.
Your car has {count} new things to try, whenever you like.
achievement: Oh, “{name}”! Your profile → achievements has it now.
achievements: {count} new achievements! See your profile → achievements.
{count} achievements at once? Your profile → achievements!
complete: Every achievement. Every one! I’m so proud of you.
All of them, done. I’m a little speechless…
100%. You did it all. I’m glowing.
wakeFirst: Mm… let me wake up first…
honeymoon: {partner} and I are away on honeymoon! Back tomorrow.
Off on our honeymoon with {partner}! Back tomorrow.
{partner} and I are taking a little trip. Back tomorrow!
challenge: {challenge}: today’s challenge. I think you can.
partner: {partner} and I make a lovely team.
{partner} was saying how smooth your rhythm is.
{partner} keeps telling me about your good runs.
{partner} is bouncing about somewhere, I expect.
{partner} and I are proud of you, for the record.
morning: Good morning. Tea first, then keys?
Oh, good morning! The home row’s all warmed up.
Good morning. {next} is ready when you are.
Morning! Nice and slow to begin.
afternoon: Afternoon. Nice time for a steady few minutes.
Good afternoon. {next} is here when you are.
Afternoon. Let’s make it a calm one.
evening: Evening. Nice to end the day with you.
Hello, evening. Let’s keep it light.
Evening! The keys are quieter now.
Evening. A few minutes, then rest.
night: Late one? Let’s keep it short and soft.
Hello, night owl. I’m awake too.
It’s late. A few keys, then sleep?
Quiet hours. Just you, me and the home row.
Mm, the night shift. Be kind to your wrists.
welcomeBack: There you are. {days} days. Welcome back.
Welcome back! Let’s ease in gently.
{days} days away. The keys didn’t go anywhere.
Oh, hello again. I saved your place.
Back after {days} days. Slow and steady, then.
Welcome home. Your fingers will remember.
personalBest: {wpm} wpm, your fastest yet. I noticed.
Oh, {wpm} wpm. That’s a new record.
New best, {wpm} wpm. I’m glowing a little.
streak: {days} days in a row. Steady does it.
Your goal, {days} days running. Lovely habit.
{days} days on the trot. Well done.
Goal met {days} days in a row. That’s care.
themeUnreadable: Hm. {what} is hard to read. A little more contrast?
I can barely make out {what}. Nudge it further from the page.
{what} is whispering. Let it speak up a bit.
Gently: {what} doesn’t stand out enough yet.
themeScheme: The page looks {page}, but the theme says {scheme}. Switch “light or dark”?
A {page} page marked {scheme}. The rest of the app will dress for the wrong one.
themeMistakes: Mistakes and typed text look alike. Give mistakes their own colour.
I can’t tell your slips from the rest. A different shade for mistakes?
themeAccent: The accent and mistakes are twins. Links will look like errors.
That accent reads like a mistake. Something calmer, perhaps?
themeLoud: That background is very bright. Kind for a moment, tiring for an hour.
Quite a loud page. Softer, and your eyes will thank you.
themeHeat: The key heat steps are out of order. They should deepen from 1 to 4.
Heat 1 to 4 should build, like a slow blush. These jump about.
themeSameAsBase: A blank page. Hover a colour and I’ll show you where it lands.
Change anything you like. I’ll say what I think.
themeLovely: That’s lovely. Gentle, and easy to read.
Mm. Everything reads well. Save it.
Nicely done. I could type on that all day.
It all passes, and it suits you.

Oh, good morning. I’m Libby. Just resting my eyes.
The light’s so soft. Hi, I’m Libby.
wake@afternoon: Mm, an afternoon doze. Hello, I’m Libby.
Oh! I lost track of the afternoon. Hi, I’m Libby.
Hello. I was only resting for a moment. I’m Libby.
wake@evening: Oh, evening already. Hello, I’m Libby.
Mm, the evening light. Hi, I’m Libby.
Good evening. I nodded off a little. I’m Libby.
wake@night: Oh, it’s night. Hello, I’m Libby. Quietly.
Mm… it’s late. I’m Libby. Nice to see you.
Still up? So am I, now. I’m Libby.
intro@morning: A morning lesson. A calm way to begin the day.
Good morning. Fresh minds make good typists.
intro@afternoon: An afternoon lesson. Take it steadily.
Good afternoon. Shall we ease into it?
A quiet afternoon for a few new keys.
intro@evening: An evening lesson. No hurry at all.
A gentle end to the day. Shall we?
Good evening. One lesson, at your own pace.
intro@night: It’s late. One careful try is plenty.
A night lesson. Soft keys, slow hands.
Late practice. Be kind to yourself tonight.
warmup@morning: A morning warm-up. Fingers wake slowly.
Gentle laps first. It’s still early.
Warm-up now, then the lesson. Good habit.
warmup@afternoon: A warm-up to reset the afternoon.
Easy laps first. Then we’ll see.
Loosen up a little, then begin.
warmup@evening: Evening warm-up. Let the day fall away.
Warm-up first. Your hands have done a lot today.
Slow laps to settle in for the evening.
warmup@night: A soft warm-up, since it’s late.
Gentle laps. No pressure at this hour.
Warm-up first. Sleepy hands need it.
sleepy@morning: Mm, still a little sleepy myself.
A pause is fine. Mornings take time.
Take a moment. I’ll be here.
sleepy@afternoon: The afternoon lull. A stretch, perhaps?
Rest a moment. It’s that time of day.
No rush. I was drifting a little too.
sleepy@evening: You’ve done a lot today. A pause is fine.
Evening tiredness. Breathe for a moment.
sleepy@night: It’s late. Sleep is a fine next step.

Rest well. The keys will keep.
